relevant.instructions: Is `title` or `text` about REA, the 'Reverse Engineer Anything' tool (github.com/morluto/rea, npm rea-agents) that lets AI coding agents reverse engineer software? Answer no when REA means something else (real estate, a person, another product) or the tool is not mentioned at all.

criteria.true: the item is about this REA reverse-engineering tool or something built with it
criteria.false: unrelated, or REA means something else

wow.instructions: How impressive and verifiable is what the author did with REA, based only on `title` and `text`? Judge the work reported, not how popular it is. News articles, reposts, opinions and link shares are the lowest level even when enthusiastic. A rebuild or finding only counts as verified when the text names tests, comparisons against the original, published code or a playable/usable result.
criteria: News, commentary, opinion, a link share, or REA is only mentioned; no hands-on work by the author
A tool, integration, plugin, package, tutorial or small experiment around REA, or a first try with no specific target
A hands-on analysis of a specific named target with a clear concrete finding (a function, rule, protocol or limitation)
A usable rebuild or an important finding on a specific target, with some evidence such as code, a commit, screenshots or a few tests
A major verified result: a playable or usable full rebuild, large test suites matching the original output, or a significant firmware or hardware finding

status.instructions: What evidence does `text` say exists for the author's claims?

criteria.tested: comparison tests against the original, evidence files, or reproducible steps are described
criteria.shipped: a public repo, commit, release, or usable output exists, without described tests
criteria.reported: only the author's own account; no code, tests or output are offered
criteria.none: not a claim of work at all (news, opinion, question)

type.instructions: What kind of item is this, based on `title` and `text`?

criteria.case: someone used REA on a specific target and reports what they found or rebuilt
criteria.app: a tool, plugin, MCP bridge, port, GUI, package or integration built around REA
criteria.learn: a tutorial, guide, course material or how-to video about using REA
criteria.news: news, review, commentary, opinion or a link share about REA
